attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The remaining Yang-Mills gap is not the finite-dimensional proof; it is proving that the actual Wilson collar-collapse admits the decomposition \(N=\Gamma\circ M+B\) with rank-one \(\Gamma\), positive additive boundary OPE \(B\), and diagonal no-defect for the locked Wilson renormalization. In particular, no current RG estimate yet proves that hairpin/cusp terms at the reflection plane are positive Gram contacts rather than indefinite pair-dependent counterterms.
steps: Start with fixed collar observables \(T_\delta F_i\). Regulated reflection positivity and RG convergence in the OS topology give \(N^{(\delta)}\ge0\) and hence a positive collar-limit matrix \(N\ge0\). This part is valid by the closed-cone argument already isolated in earlier cycles.

Write the most general finite Wilson trace relation being tested as \(N=\Gamma\circ M+B\), separating pairwise multiplicative boundary factors from additive reflection-plane contacts. The target OS positivity problem is to infer \(M\ge0\) from \(N\ge0\) without changing the theory.

If \(\Gamma\) is rank-one, \(\Gamma_{ij}=\overline{d_i}d_j\), then \(\Gamma\circ M=D^*MD\). This is an invertible congruence and preserves/refects positivity once \(D\) is fixed by the locked observable normalization.

For the additive term, assume it is a positive boundary Gram matrix and that diagonal trace continuity has already removed individual defects. Then \(B\ge0\) and \(B_{ii}=0\) imply \(B_{ij}=0\) for every \(i,j\) by Cauchy-Schwarz. Hence \(B=0\), not merely harmless.
With \(B=0\), positivity transfers by \(M=(D^*)^{-1}ND^{-1}\ge0\). This completes the finite-matrix bridge under the stated assumptions.

To test necessity, examine a normalized two-observable multiplicative anomaly \(\Gamma=\begin{pmatrix}1&\beta\\\overline\beta&1\end{pmatrix}\). If \(0<|\beta|<1\), then \(\Gamma\ge0\), but \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) is not positive; entrywise recovery of \(M\) can destroy OS positivity. Thus nonfactorizing mixed damping is a real falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument is a valid bridge theorem conditional on a precise boundary-value/OPE statement. It does not yet prove the needed Yang-Mills analytic estimate for nonlocal Wilson loops as reflected supports collide at \(t=0\), nor does it establish OS-density of the Wilson/composite core after this trace operation.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: finite OS-matrix boundary defects

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity holds: for every cutoff pair \((a,L)\), every finite positive-time family \(G_i\), and coefficients \(c_i\), \(\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta G_i,G_j)\ge0\).
The RG cutoff-removal topology is strong enough to pass every fixed-collar reflected matrix entry to the continuum, so \(N^{(\delta)}\ge0\) and \(N^{(\delta)}\to N\) imply \(N\ge0\).
For the chosen finite locked Wilson/composite family, the collar trace limit exists and decomposes as \(N=\Gamma\circ M+B\).
The multiplicative anomaly is a diagonal congruence, \(amma_{ij}=\overline{d_i}d_j\), already included in the fixed normalization of the same observables.
The additive boundary contact sector is reflection-positive as a finite matrix \(B\ge0\), and individual trace continuity gives \(B_{ii}=0\) for every test observable in the family.
definitions: source object: a directed family of regulated reflection-positive Schwinger functionals \(S_{a,L}\) on a fixed gauge-invariant observable algebra, with collar approximants \(T_\delta F\) supported in \(t>\delta\).

target object: the continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) restricted to the same positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, encoded by finite OS matrices \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) whose positivity reconstructs the OS Hilbert space.

controlled interface: the two-step passage \(S_{a,L}\to S\) for fixed collars, followed by \(\delta\downarrow0\) in finite reflected quadratic forms, with possible boundary trace factors recorded as \(N=\Gamma\circ M+B\).

same-theory condition: the observables \(F_i\) and their collar approximants \(T_\delta F_i\) use the same locked Wilson-loop/composite renormalization; allowed multiplicative factors must be pre-existing diagonal congruences, and no additive boundary field may be added to redefine the target algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A concrete falsifier is a pair of Wilson observables with either a nonzero additive mixed contact while all diagonal contacts vanish, forcing the contact matrix not to be positive, or a pair-dependent multiplicative anomaly \(\Gamma_{ij}\ne\overline{d_i}d_j\) that cannot be absorbed by the locked same-theory normalization.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma turns the informal phrase no-new-boundary-renormalization into a finite-dimensional positivity-reflection criterion. It shows that a positive additive contact term is harmless once diagonal trace continuity is proved; the remaining dangerous anomalies are nonfactorizing multiplicative terms or indefinite additive contacts.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite Wilson OS-matrix defect criterion. Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_n\) be locked gauge-invariant positive-time Wilson/composite observables and let \(T_\delta F_i\) be collar-separated approximants. Suppose the collar OS matrices \(N^{(\delta)}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) have a positive limit \(N\), and suppose the boundary trace relation has the finite-matrix form \(N=\Gamma\circ M+B\), where \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) is the intended continuum OS matrix, \(\Gamma\) is a multiplicative boundary anomaly, and \(B\) is an additive contact matrix. If \(\Gamma_{ij}=\overline{d_i}d_j\) with all \(d_i\ne0\), and if \(B\ge0\) with \(B_{ii}=0\) for every locked observable, then \(M\ge0\). Thus OS positivity is valid for the intended target theory under rank-one multiplicative renormalization plus diagonal-killed positive additive contact.

assumptions: The additive contact term vanishes or has already been killed by the criterion of cycle-0184-L1.
All relevant finite matrices are Hermitian and the anomaly matrix has nonzero entries.
The intended same-theory passage must not rely on changing the observable algebra after taking the collar limit.
definitions: \(\Gamma\circ M\) denotes the Hadamard product, representing pairwise multiplicative boundary/cusp factors in reflected Wilson pairings.
\(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) is the entrywise reciprocal matrix, defined only when all \(\Gamma_{ij}\ne0\).
A positive Schur multiplier means \(A\ge0\Rightarrow \Gamma^{[-1]}\circ A\ge0\) on every finite matrix generated by the locked test family.

equations.valid_when: The boundary relation is purely multiplicative and every anomaly entry is nonzero.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A normalized mixed damping factor \(|\beta|<1\) gives the standard two-by-two falsifier: choose positive \(N\) for which \(M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\) has negative determinant.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates nonfactorizing Wilson cusp or hairpin damping as a genuine same-theory obstruction, not merely a normalization ambiguity.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Reciprocal Schur multiplier test for multiplicative Wilson anomalies. If collar limits satisfy \(N=\Gamma\circ M\) with no additive contact, then positivity of every collar-limit matrix \(N\ge0\) implies positivity of the intended target matrix \(M\) for all finite tests exactly when the entrywise reciprocal \(\Gamma^{[-1]}=(1/\Gamma_{ij})\) is a positive Schur multiplier on the relevant finite OS matrix cone. If, in addition, normalized \(\Gamma\) is itself a positive boundary kernel with \(\Gamma_{ii}=1\) and positive entries, this condition forces \(\Gamma_{ij}=\overline{d_i}d_j\) with \(|d_i|=1\), hence no nontrivial mixed damping is allowed.

assumptions: The contact term is additive: \(N=M+B\), after any allowed diagonal multiplicative congruence has been removed.
The boundary contribution is positive semidefinite for each finite family.
The diagonal entries of the additive contact term vanish by already-proved single-observable trace continuity.
definitions: A boundary OPE contribution is a finite matrix \(B_{ij}\) obtained from the coefficients of reflection-plane fields appearing in \(\Theta T_\delta F_i\cdot T_\delta F_j\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
Diagonal trace continuity means \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta T_\delta F,T_delta F)=S(\Theta F,F)\) after the locked renormalization of the same observable \(F\).

Positive boundary OPE means the extracted contact coefficients form a positive semidefinite matrix for every finite family, as would happen if they are vacuum Gram pairings of genuine boundary fields.

equations.valid_when: The same positive boundary OPE controls both diagonal and mixed reflected pairings.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a Wilson hairpin/cusp family with zero diagonal additive defect but nonzero mixed additive defect; that would be a falsifier of positive boundary OPE compatibility and would break the current bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma narrows the remaining obstruction. A mixed additive contact can only survive if it is not part of a positive boundary Gram sector or if diagonal trace continuity has failed.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Diagonal trace continuity plus positive boundary OPE kills additive contacts. In the collar-collapse analysis of reflected Wilson products, if the boundary OPE contribution is representable as a Gram matrix of reflection-plane fields and each individual observable has a valid same-theory trace limit, then every mixed additive boundary contact vanishes automatically. Therefore the analytic estimate needed for additive terms can be reduced to proving positivity of the boundary OPE sector and diagonal no-defect, rather than separately estimating every mixed entry.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if a concrete Wilson hairpin/cusp calculation exhibits nonrank-one mixed damping or an indefinite mixed additive contact under the locked renormalization; that would show the current OS bridge proves the wrong theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves, for a dense Wilson/composite core, fixed-collar RG convergence plus a boundary trace theorem with rank-one multiplicative factors, positive boundary OPE contacts, and diagonal no-defect.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced new mathematical compression: additive contacts can be killed by diagonal no-defect if they are positive, so the next analytic target is more specific than before. The closed-cone step remains valid but secondary.

dependency_updates.description: The formal bridge is now: fixed-collar RG convergence gives \(N\ge0\); the boundary trace map must be positivity-reflecting. This is guaranteed by rank-one multiplicative congruence plus diagonal-killed positive additive contact.

The algebra must be locked strongly enough that individual Wilson renormalizations define diagonal factors before the OS limit; pair-dependent cusp factors are excluded unless shown to be rank-one congruences.

The topology still needs convergence of every finite reflected collar matrix entry. The new information is that the topology alone is insufficient unless the collar-to-plane trace map has a positivity-reflecting inverse.
To rule out additive mixed defects efficiently, prove that reflection-plane contact terms form positive Gram matrices and that their diagonal entries vanish under locked single-loop trace continuity.

falsifiers: falsifier: a two-loop reflected Wilson family with normalized multiplicative anomaly \(\Gamma_{11}=\Gamma_{22}=1\), \(0<|\Gamma_{12}|<1\), because the reciprocal Schur multiplier then fails the two-by-two positivity test.

falsifier: an additive mixed contact matrix with \(B_{11}=B_{22}=0\) but \(B_{12}\ne0\); such a term cannot be positive semidefinite and would show that boundary contacts are not a valid positive Gram sector.
falsifier: diagonal collar trace failure for a single locked Wilson observable, since then additive boundary fields have already changed the target theory before any mixed OS test is considered.

falsifier: a required boundary counterterm or cusp-renormalization ratio depending on the pair \((F_i,F_j)\) rather than on individual observables, since this violates the same-theory condition and cannot be absorbed by diagonal congruence.

falsifier: RG compactness estimates that converge on ordinary Euclidean correlators but not on reflected collar probes \(S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\), because then the closed-cone transfer is not valid for the needed OS matrices.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 184 separates additive and multiplicative boundary anomalies more sharply. A positive additive contact is not an independent mixed obstruction once diagonal trace continuity is known: by Cauchy-Schwarz, zero diagonal forces the whole contact matrix to vanish. Therefore a surviving mixed additive defect would itself be a falsifier of positive boundary OPE compatibility. The genuinely dangerous Wilson anomalies are now narrowed to nonrank-one multiplicative damping or indefinite pair-dependent contacts. This turns the previous no-new-boundary-renormalization slogan into a concrete finite OS-matrix theorem with a valid linear-algebra proof and a precise Yang-Mills analytic gap.
